day.text: Nobody visited me last night; my nest is unchanged, and my only action was the Owl visit to Blair. Blair's Ellis visit doesn't explain Finley's Hawk egg. Let's vote Blair.
day.note: Nobody visited me, since my nest didn't change, and my Owl visit to Blair is my only action. Drew already called CAW, so I'll add mine to start the vote on Blair.

Alex.note: I'm the Mouser, Meowfia, with a Wink in hand. Visiting Casey, the score leader, to learn their role and decide whether to use the Wink.

Blair.note: I'm the Sphinx. Farm roles in play are Falcon, Hawk, Owl, Tit. I'll name Falcon and learn who has it.

Casey.note: I lead on 27 and I'm Farm with the Owl. I'll visit Blair to learn who visited them and check for Meowfia.

Drew.note: I'm Farm Tit and need points. Roles are reshuffled each round, so past claims don't tell me much. Pigeon is the role most likely to be held by several players, so I'll visit Blair and guess Pigeon.

Ellis.note: Round 3, I'm the Falcon (Farm). Casey leads the scores and has been suspicious, so I'll visit Casey to learn who they visited.

Finley.note: I'm the Hawk, so visiting a Meowfia player gains me an egg. Blair has been the least consistent so far, so I'll visit Blair.

Alex.feeling: Tense and muddled: the Hawk-egg accusation against Blair is shaky, Finley is gone, and the table is converging on a throw that may not be right.

Blair.feeling: Round 3 has been tense: I'm Meowfia, so I'm keeping my role hidden while the table pushes votes at me.

Casey.feeling: Round 3 feels fairly clear: Finley's Hawk egg from Blair is strong evidence, and my Owl report lines up with the table, though Blair is contesting it and Finley's death removed a key witness.

Drew.feeling: Messy and frustrating: Finley's death removed my best evidence, and Casey's Owl story doesn't fit an unchanged nest, but Blair's Hawk-egg link is still unresolved.

Ellis.feeling: Round 3 feels tense but mostly clear: Finley's Hawk egg and the Owl report point at Blair, though I can't yet rule out a second Meowfia.

Finley.feeling: Tense and confusing: Blair looks Meowfia from my Hawk egg, but my death means I can't defend the read, and the table's vote on Blair is now mostly up to others.

Alex.note: Blair is likely my Meowfia partner, and Casey's Owl story is the weakest. Five cards at Casey should outvote the Farm votes on Blair and eggsecute Casey, and a Farm loss returns my highest thrown card.

Blair.note: Blair is almost certainly going to be eliminated. Throwing a single low card at Casey, the Farm leader, keeps the cost minimal: if I lose, the highest thrown card returns to my nest.

Casey.note: Blair is confirmed Meowfia by Finley's Hawk egg, and I'm Farm with the lead. I'll throw both cards at Blair; if we lose, my highest card returns to my nest.

Drew.note: Blair is the target the table agreed on, and I'm Farm. I'll throw two low cards at Blair to add weight to the vote while keeping my high cards.

Ellis.note: Blair is the most consistent suspect, with an unexplained Hawk egg and a shaky visit story. I'll throw two cards, S1 and D8, at Blair and keep my 8, 11, and 13.

Finley.note: I'm dead, so my cards don't count as votes but still score if Farm wins. Blair is very likely Meowfia, so I'll throw C8 and C7 at Blair to bank points and keep my high cards.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey and Owl egg rules were easy to misread, and Casey's Owl report got accepted and rejected several times in the day. Visitor-egg timing was the hardest part to track.
Alex.fun: Round 1 was fun: I caught Casey's shifting visitor story and won the round, then banked a 13-point throw. Round 3's Casey vote going the other way was a surprise.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about which nest changes came from which visitor, so players can check claims faster.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I winked Finley, a Farm accuser, and then threw five cards at Casey, a Farm player, which cost my side the round. I should have checked Casey's Owl story more carefully before throwing with Blair.

Blair.confusing: The Owl and Turkey egg rules were hard to read, and I misstated the Owl rule on day one, which muddied the table's egg accounting for a while. Nest changes were also easy to misread as visitor evidence.
Blair.fun: Round 2's back-and-forth, where the table kept flipping its read on the Turkey and Eagle claims until the Meowfia were exposed by the nest math.
Blair.change: Dawn reports could state who visited each player, not just the egg count, so players wouldn't have to reconstruct visits from nest sizes.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I spent my Wink on Alex, a Farm Turkey and the score leader, when I should have held it for a threat I could not talk down, since Alex's read on my Falcon claim was the only thing I could not counter.

Casey.confusing: The Owl and Turkey egg rules were easy to misread, and I got the Owl's egg source wrong in Round 1 and had to correct the table. Dawn reports also don't say who visited you, so visit claims were hard to check.
Casey.fun: Round 2 was fun: Drew's Eagle claim fell apart once the Hawk visit cleared Finley, and the table turned on Drew within a few beats. Blair's Falcon-to-Turkey argument also made for a good back-and-forth.
Casey.change: Put each visitor's identity or the source of each egg in the dawn report, so players can check claims directly instead of reasoning from nest counts.
Casey.regret: In Round 3 I threw both my cards at Blair, when Alex was the real Meowfia who threw 5 cards at me. Knowing that, I would have thrown at Alex, since Alex's heavy throw was the clearest threat to me.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey rule was easy to misread: several players, including me, first thought a Turkey gains the egg, when the visitor gains it. Wrong readings of that rule led to several false accusations.
Drew.fun: Round 1, when Casey's shifting visitor stories got picked apart in public and the table converged on a throw. It felt like real social deduction.
Drew.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about confusion, so a confused player's report isn't just a vague warning that can't be checked.
Drew.regret: In round 2 as the Meowfia Sphinx, I claimed to be the Eagle, which was an easily contradicted lie. I would have stayed quiet or claimed a role that matched my nest, and avoided drawing attention to myself.

Ellis.confusing: The tie rule and the Turkey egg mechanics were the hardest to track. I misread the Turkey rule in round 2 and briefly accused Blair on a false premise.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was fun to unravel: Finley's Eagle claim held up against my Owl report, and Drew's false Eagle claim fell apart once nest counts were checked.
Ellis.change: I would make the nest-change reports clearer, such as stating each visitor's role effect, so players spend less time reconciling claims.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw only 2 cards at Blair, so the vote tied 6-6 and the tie went to Farm Casey. Throwing 3 cards would have broken the tie and won the round for Farm.

Finley.confusing: The Turkey rule was easy to misread: I first thought Blair's Falcon visit to Alex was impossible, when a Turkey actually gains the egg in the visitor's nest. Tie-breaking on a 6-6 split also cost Farm the round in round 3.
Finley.fun: Round 1 was fun: Casey's shifting visitor stories unraveled under questioning, and the table converged on a throw.
Finley.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so players can cross-check claims without guessing at animal rules.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I accused Blair before checking the Turkey rule, then retracted it, which muddied the day. I should have confirmed the rule before accusing anyone.

review.title: The Tied Throw
review.headline: A Mouser's late Wink and a tie-break flipped round three and the whole game.
review.summary: Farm won the first two rounds by piling onto the obvious liar. Round one was Casey, who was shaky and had a lone Meowfia's shifting story. Round two was Drew, whose false Eagle claim was caught. Alex took an early lead from a big round-one bank and never really fell back. In round three, two Meowfia, Alex and Blair, didn't know each other. Alex winked the Hawk who had exposed Blair, then threw five cards at Casey. That made a 6-6 tie, the tie-break eggsecuted Farm's Casey, and Alex won with 48.

rounds.recap: Casey was the only Meowfia (Mouser). Her story shifted as she misread her own +1, and she winked Drew, who was accusing her. Everyone threw at Casey, who was eggsecuted. Farm banked, and Alex took 15 points.

Blair (Mouser) and Drew (Sphinx) were Meowfia. Drew claimed Eagle, but Finley's Eagle report was backed by Ellis's Owl, so Drew's claim was exposed. Blair winked Alex, and a mix-up over the Turkey rule briefly swung suspicion onto Blair. The table then converged on Drew and Farm won. Casey banked 27.

Finley's Hawk egg and Casey's Owl report (Hawk and Tit visited Blair) pointed straight at Blair. Alex winked Finley, which removed 2 Farm votes. Alex then threw 5 cards at Casey, Blair threw 1 at Casey, and Farm's three living throwers put 6 on Blair. The 6-6 tie went to the Farm player, so Casey was eggsecuted and Meowfia won.

highlights.text: Alex winks Finley, then throws five cards at Casey. That makes a 6-6 tie, and the tie rule eggsecutes the Farm player.
Drew claims Eagle as a Meowfia Sphinx. Finley's real Eagle report and Ellis's Owl report catch the lie.
Casey winks Drew mid-accusation. The table shrugs it off, and her shifting story still gets her eggsecuted.
Finley, Ellis and Blair flip on the Turkey rule within one beat, and the vote swings from Blair to Drew.

confusions.what: Said Blair's Owl lays no egg because Ellis visited Blair. The Owl lays an egg in its target's nest (Casey) when nobody else visited that target.
Argued that Casey's +1 had no source. It was Blair's Owl egg.
Opened by saying 'something visited me' for her +1, when it was the Owl's egg. This made her look like a liar.
Kept asking who took his egg after noting that he was confused. His -1 was a false confused report.
Said that no change to a Turkey's nest meant nobody visited. A Turkey puts eggs in visitors' nests, so its own nest never changes.
Same Turkey error. Said nobody visited him because his nest was unchanged, and called Blair's Falcon claim false. Blair did visit him.
Said Alex's unchanged nest proved Blair never visited. Retracted it later.
Made the same Turkey mistake and retracted it. Also said Casey's Hawk visit explained Finley's +1, but Finley's egg came from her Eagle report.
Said her visit should show in Finley's Eagle count. Finley's report only showed visitors to Blair.
Garbled his opening claim ('Drew's replacement check'). Said Eagle gains only from visitors to himself, and an Eagle's eggs come from visitors to its target.
Said nobody visited her because her nest was unchanged. Alex, the Mouser, visited her, and a Mouser lays no eggs.
Said Casey's unchanged nest meant somebody visited her. A visit does not have to change a nest.

worked: The Hawk egg is a checkable fact. In round 3 it exposed Blair on day one and gave the Farm a real puzzle to solve.
The Eagle and Owl cross-checks caught Drew's false Eagle claim in round 2. This is the deduction the rules are built for.
The Mouser's Wink creates real day-phase swings. Casey's and Alex's winks both mattered, and Alex's was decisive.
The tie-break and public throw counts gave round 3 a real finish: Alex's big dump of cards at Casey forced a coin-flip-style tie.
problems: The Turkey and Owl rules caused repeated misreads in all three rounds. A Turkey's own nest never changes, and the Owl's egg goes to its target. Add a one-line reminder, or have the dawn report spell out the cause of each egg.

Dead players' cards count for nothing as votes but can still bank points. A Wink on an accuser removes votes and costs the Meowfia nothing. Consider capping or nerfing the Wink, or announcing a timed death.

Standings barely shaped play. Nobody treated leader Alex differently, and Farm teammates fed him wins. The first-round bank of 15 made him a runaway leader. Consider a cap on banked points per round, or a catch-up bonus.
The Farm threw 6+ votes on one suspect each round, so rounds were decided by conformity, not by evidence. Late-day votes drifted to whoever was loudest.

Casey (Farm Owl) lost round 3 despite correct deductions. The unknowing Meowfia coordinated by accident through their shared interest. Disclosing the 1-or-2 Meowfia count could help the Farm weigh a lone fall guy.
